candidates: Drug-induced blepharitis and ectropion associated with TNF-α inhibitors
key_facts: Switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable
champion: Drug-induced blepharitis and ectropion associated with TNF-α inhibitors

raw.champion: Drug-induced blepharitis and ectropion associated with TNF-α inhibitors
raw.rationale: The patient's history of treatment with TNF-α inhibitors (infliximab and adalimumab) and the development of bilateral eyelid involvement, ectropion, and crusty plaques on the eyelid margins, which are consistent with the described images showing resolution after treatment discontinuation, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Psoriasiform blepharitis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of an autoimmune disease, the specific findings and the temporal relationship with TNF-α inhibitor treatment better support a drug-induced condition rather than a psoriasiform blepharitis.

rejected.label: Chronic anterior blepharitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and the presence of ectropion, which is not typically a feature of chronic anterior blepharitis, along with the improvement after discontinuation of TNF-α inhibitors, make this diagnosis less likely.
